methods.label: Classify the choices
methods.explanation: \(22/7\) is a fraction, \(0.101\) is a terminating decimal, and \(\sqrt{16}=4\) is an integer, so all are rational. \(\pi\) is a nonterminating, nonrepeating decimal, so it is irrational.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 7 number classification and the principal square root of a perfect square.

candidate.annotationRationale: Recognizing the irrational choice is the assessed target cnm_077. The rational-number definition supports classifying fractions and integers (cnm_003); evaluating √16 is local supporting knowledge (cnm_075). A second classification pass would repeat the same idea. review.mathematicalCheck: 22/7 is a ratio of integers with nonzero denominator, 0.101=101/1000, and √16=4. These are rational, while π is irrational, making D the unique answer.
